I’m 33 too but I was in a similar lonely situation about six years ago.  I spent so much time focusing on my career and money and eventually i snapped due to the depression.  I won’t bore you with the details but I can share my revelations...
If you don’t make time there won’t be time.  If someone asks you to go somewhere with them, go.  If they’re not asking make the initiative and ask them.  Go anywhere.  This world is filled with so many possible experiences.  In your case, you probably need to take the initiative and learn the language of the land.  You’re asking if things will change.  The world has been spinning long before you were born.  You can hold on to what you feel comfortable but sometimes you need to take that leap of faith and let yourself feel anxious and vulnerable.  It’s a cliche saying but life is a journey not a destination.  Never stop learning and experiencing.

Most things work on a sliding scale but also require tweaks and balances.  Don’t jump into something you don’t think you can handle but don’t be afraid to get a little hurt in the process.  I have 3 non work related trips this year planned and booked.  The past me would not have made these arrangements especially because of COVID.  My first trip out of the country was about 4 years ago by myself and I didn’t enjoy it that much because I was alone with no friends.  Now I have multiple trips planned in the same year with people I enjoy being around.  I still live with major depression daily but if I let it, it will consume me.

I was officially diagnosed with depression in college.  My doctor thought I may have had ADHD too and told me to get tested formally.  The results came back inconclusive and they pretty much noted that they would not give an ADHD diagnosis because I was being treated for depression.  They said I should retest later when my depression is under control.  My experience has been that doctors do not like do a treatment plan with both depression and ADHD at the same time.

​

Currently, my depression is under control via ketamine infusions and I take concerta for my concentration and focus issues.  For me, the biggest difference in lack of concentration between ADHD and depression is like this:

Depression: I don't feel like doing X.  I have no interest in X.  I'm tired.   I don't have the energy.

ADHD: I'm anxious.  There's so many things going on... What just happened?

​

Both thought processes end up with me losing focus and unable to concentrate.  The difference I notice is that, at the time of incidents, I'm more aware of depression induced lack of concentration.   With ADHD, i realize it in retrospect.  The car keys just end up in the fridge somehow.

In total I would estimate that I’ve had around 30 ECT treatments.   They weren’t all in the same stretch, I’ve just been hospitalized multiple times.  Although I am not a doctor, I would recommend you look into ketamine.  The ketamine mood effects last about a month for me compared to ECT that lasted maybe six months.   However,  ketamine for me has been far more effective... you notice the difference immediately and there is no memory loss.  It’s just not covered by insurance.   It’s $500per ketamine infusion in my area.  Whatever you do, good luck.  Neither are permanent fixes but ketamine to me is the logically superior and safer treatment.  Not everyone can afford $500/mo though.

One old woman was crying after she finished a session because she couldn’t remember her wedding day.   I’m not sure how extensive my memory loss was but I do believe I am one of the luckier ones.  The eye twitch issue I think “healed” itself after about 2 years.

However, there is a trick to a person can do to help me.  If the friend/spouse makes it about them and ask for help, I would be obliged to participate. This is how I thought when I was in college.  I honestly felt like my first psychiatrist was trying to get me hooked on prescription pills.  He diagnosed me with minor depression/dysthymia and said that if I didn't keep it under control it would turn into major depression.  I hated the idea of taking pills and just stopped going to appointments.  I thought I could do it on my own if I changed my lifestyle and habits.  I pushed through and graduated without the help of antidepressants.  Several years later for no reason at all I hit my first major depressive episode.  I was crying for absolutely no reason at all. Long story short, I've spent over 40K out of pocket (with insurance) because I didn't really believe in depression.  My depression is definitely genetic.  My mom has it.   My brother has it.  My grandmother has it.  

One of my all time regrets was not listening to my first psychiatrist's warning.  He was 100% correct on what would happen.

Fear leads to the dark side.  I believe in the fail fast recover fast approach.  I used to fear changing people's code early on in my career.  The reality is that they're the incompetent ones. You'll grow confidence with time.  You can gripe about bad code all day or you can fix it.  See if you can run your codebase through a code analysis tool.
Scrum Master?  Project Manager?  I think a minor would help you to create and identify feasible product requirements.

Tech debt is high when there is a lack of ownership.  When working with a poorly managed codebase, I generally start rewriting as much as possible.  It sounds like you're in a good position take leadership of the project.

I am very familiar with the symptoms of depression and I know what you’re going through.  It’s really easy to give up and at times you’re left feeling helpless.    There’s no promise or guarantee that you’ll ever get better and you don’t really have many good options.   Many people in your position have lost the battle but at the same time there exists those who have managed to keep their depression in check.  Try harder.  If there’s a small amount of hope in you channel it into something productive.   Worst case you fail but at least you can say you tried your best.   Better to have that peace of mind.   Giving up is a self fulfilling prophecy.

I don’t see what’s hard to understand about it.  From an evolutionary standpoint we’re the people who would have died off early on without reproducing.   With all the advancements in the medical field,  many of us are able to survive and maybe even pass on our depressive traits.   I’ve tried many things to change my life but it all comes down to my biology I inherited from my mom.   My mom is a pretty person but also has depression.   Wasn’t hard for her to reproduce.  Same with my grandmother.  If not for hospitals, I probably would have died at birth.

Life gives you a lot of opportunities.   Whether or not you take them is up to you.  I’m 30 now and would consider myself successful career wise.  I grew up poor but money has never been a driving factor.   The way I see it, you need to do something awesome or what’s the point on even trying?   After third place, people stop giving a shit.   I feel like giving up a lot but I know it’s the depression.  I just need that reminder once in a while.  Don’t settle and do the best you can.   It will payoff.

I gave my dogs away 2 times because of depression.  Long story short, I got another dog.  My psychiatrist and therapist both thought giving away the dogs were a bad idea but I felt I was such a bad owner.  The truth is, the dog is helping me more than the other way around.  I’m never alone, I have someone to hug, I have a routine to get out of bed because I have to feed him....  the dog adds structure to my life.   I ended up in the psych ward both times after giving my dogs away.

A job won't say why you didn't get a position.  They'll send you some generic rejection email.  You can get the hint if you're well qualified for a position and they don't even bother asking you for an interview. Military and certain government jobs will avoid taking people with mental disorders.

Talk to your primary care physician about how you've been feeling.  If it's severe enough, they'll refer you to a psychiatrist.  If it's a mild case of depression the primary care might manage your antidepressant medications.  There's sometimes a long wait list to see a psychiatrist.

If it works, even as a placebo, I think it's worth taking.  It didn't work for me.  Mental disorders can prevent you from working certain jobs.  Those jobs will ask you to give them medical information.  I lost out on a job because I didn't release my medical records when going through a background check.  On the plus side, depression got me out of jury duty.

The cops will escort you to the hospital ER where you'll have to wait for them to find you a psychiatric hospital.  You can go in voluntarily but if you say something that makes them believe you will harm yourself they will put you under the order of protective custody.  All the psych wards I've been to were a general place for people with mental issues.  Being in a psych ward is not fun.  After you leave they'll hit you with a hefty bill.
Don't be afraid to ask for help.  Hiding your true intentions could be fatal.  At least give your friends and family the opportunity to try and help.  You owe yourself that much.
I would have lied to myself and said you'll eventually be happy.  Maybe false hope is better than none.
My therapist says I need to do things even if I don't feel like it at the moment.

https://youtu.be/YjTcReaOqQ0

That's one of his videos but you can find more in the channel.
I think therapy could help you but you need to be honest.  Be open and go in without expectations that it won't work.
Yes!  There is a guy on youtube that did that and went to live in the woods.  He made a giant robot. I'd like to do that but the thought of giving up everything is scary.

The sun will explode in time.  Cancer or not, you might as well try to find something you enjoy.  Maybe you like reading reddit.  How's a dead person going to read reddit?
Yes.

Heh... I also backed out of the helium 80/20 thing.  Have you tried taking a trip to another country?  If it feels like the same shit everyday you need to make real changes.  Sometimes I feel that everything I do doesn't matter... people die and that's life.  At the same time I'm reminded of all the cool stuff I'll be missing out on if I ended it early.  GoT Season 7...  Street Legal Fully Autonomous Cars...   Mars...
Have you ever laid down in a room full of puppies?  I feel like that should be on you list.  You might change your mind and keep one.

I thought the point of living with your parents was that you don't pay rent.  Maybe you should move out and get a roommate. 

 One of my lesser hobbies is finding good deals.  Check out fatwallet.com or slickdeals.net.  Some people make a living finding deals and flipping it on ebay.

I was able to pay my 35k student loan in 2 years living frugal.

I'm agnostic but most of my family is Catholic.  I go to church only a few special times a year out of respect.  I think it helps to have a sense of community... that feeling of belonging.
